reason: The cited evidence (E1, E3) strongly supports that ultra-rapid cooling yields an amorphous structure, but it provides no data on the metastability of this amorphous phase upon reheating, the effects of sub-Tg annealing, or the relationship between structural relaxation and thermal stability. The key premises regarding annealing and its outcomes are entirely unsupported by the provided passages.
premises: Ultra-rapid quenching (10^5-10^6 K/s) can bypass primary crystallization and form an amorphous structure in this alloy.
The as-quenched amorphous state is metastable and prone to crystallization upon reheating.
Sub-Tg annealing promotes structural relaxation (reducing internal stresses and stored enthalpy) without triggering crystallization.
Structural relaxation increases the thermal stability of the amorphous phase, raising the crystallization onset temperature.
The combination of rapid quenching and sub-Tg annealing yields a higher amorphous fraction and more homogeneous glassy microstructure than rapid quenching alone.
